rule: ORD-02 / ORD-03, BR-ORD-2, BR-ORD-3, BR-PRD-8, BR-PRD-9
description:
What one order line costs once its promotion and tax are applied. This is the arithmetic the three resolvers stop short of: they answer *which* price, *which* promotion and *which* rate apply, and this turns those into the four numbers a document shows. See ../README.md for the format rules — money and percentages are strings, so neither language parses a float on the way in.

The promotion here is already **resolved**: a tiered promotion arrives with its winning tier's discount projected onto percentOff/amountOff, because PromotionResolver settles that contest before this runs. A null promotion means none applied; a null taxPercentage means this tenant has no rate for the product's class and country, which is deliberately a different fact from a rate of zero.

cases.name: no promotion and no tax is just the multiplication
tax is charged on the discounted net, not the subtotal
cases.why: The rule the whole ordering exists for. Taxing the subtotal would charge the shopkeeper for 20.00 nobody paid.

cases.name: a fixed amount comes off the line, not off each unit
cases.why: Both readings are defensible and differ by the quantity. '5 off' on a line of twelve is 5, not 60 — which is what a shopkeeper hears, and what keeps a fixed-amount promotion bounded as the order grows.

cases.name: a discount larger than the line gives the line away rather than paying the shop
cases.why: Unclamped this lands at -2.00 and the order total falls as the shopkeeper buys more. Refusing instead would strand an order over a promotion the rep did not choose and cannot edit, which BR-ORD-9 exists to avoid.

cases.name: a bundle discounts whole groups and charges the remainder in full
cases.why: Buy 2 get 1 on a line of 14 is four complete groups of three: four units free, two left over paid for. Rounding groups up would give away stock the shopkeeper did not buy enough to earn.

cases.name: a bundle the quantity does not reach discounts nothing
cases.why: Two units against 'buy 2 get 1' is not one group — the group is three.

cases.name: a fractional quantity earns only the whole bundles it reaches
cases.why: Where a weight-based unit of measure meets a count-based promotion. 6.5 kg earns the same free weight as 6 kg — half a free kilo is not what the author meant — but the extra half is still charged.

cases.name: a cross-product bundle discounts nothing on this line
cases.why: 'Buy six of these, get one of those free' puts the discount on a line this function cannot see. BR-ORD-3 calls the line-level promotion line-level; crediting it here would balance the order total while putting the money against the wrong product for every report downstream. The order-level pass applies it.

cases.name: every step rounds half up rather than to even
cases.why: BR-PRD-9. 3 x 3.335 is 10.005, a half-cent: banker's rounding gives 10.00 and half-up gives 10.01. Chosen because the two policies disagree here — at 10.015 they agree and the case would pass against either.

cases.name: a percentage discount rounds before it is taxed
cases.why: 12.5% of 13.93 is 1.74125, which rounds to 1.74. Carrying the untruncated figure into the tax step would give a different cent on the total, and the four printed numbers would not add up.

cases.name: a zero-decimal currency rounds to whole units
cases.why: JPY has no minor unit, so every step lands on an integer. A calculation hard-coded to two decimals passes every EUR case in this file and fails here.
